description: Per-object-type descriptor. InitObject (game/src/object.c) copies the start-state function, the copy ability and the hit points into the new Object; ObjectInitSprite / the VRAM helpers take the tile budget, palette and animation list from it; ObjectMain awards the score from it when the object dies. 194 read sites in game/src (MODDING.md R0: OBJ_DESC()). It is the main per-type tuning table: hp, score and ability are plain numbers here. Boss/mini-boss hit points (types 0x38..0x52) are NOT taken from it; see tuning_inventory.json boss.hp.
notes: The table is ROM-resident (PORT: replaced by port/rom_data.h, game/include/data.h:790); it is the manifest kind obj_desc (assets/manifest.json), served as objects/types.json.
unk10 and unk14 are ROM pointers (function / AnimInfo array); a served copy needs them relocated or rebound (MODDING.md: Res_ServedAddr).
Several fields are shared by unrelated item types with different meanings: for food items unk4 is the heal amount (it becomes Object.unk80 like hp).

fields.name: hurtAnimSlot
fields.description: Index into the unk14 AnimInfo list (Object.unk83 is the current animation slot) used for the 'hurt'/stunned pose. Damage, inhale and knock-back paths set obj->unk83 to unk0 or (randomly) unk1; kirby.c's inhale/carry check and cookin/parasol test unk83 >= unk0 to mean 'currently in the hurt pose'. Mega Titan uses it when it takes a hit.

evidence.note: random choice between unk0 and unk1 after a hit
unk83 indexes the unk14 AnimInfo list

evidence.data: unk1 == unk0+1 in 55 of 219 rows and unk1 == unk0 in 163 (114 rows are 0/0: types without a hurt pose); max 29
evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

stats.summary: 0..29; 0 for items, gadgets, doors and most bosses' children

fields.name: hurtAnimSlotAlt
fields.description: Second hurt-pose animation slot; after a hit the engine picks unk0 or unk1 at random (Rand16() & 1). Usually unk0+1 (the mirrored/alternate pose) or equal to unk0.

fields.name: score
fields.description: Score awarded to the Kirby that dealt the killing blow (Object.unk86) when the object is destroyed with hp <= 0. Dark Mind's final form adds it from its own code.

evidence.data: values are round score amounts: 0,50,100,150,200,...,1000,1500,2000,5000,20000 (bosses), 30000 (Dark Meta Knight), 60000 (Dark Mind)
evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

fields.name: hp
fields.description: Starting hit points (copied to Object.unk80) for every type except the boss/mini-boss range 0x38..0x52, which take theirs from gUnk_08351530 / gUnk_08351608 scaled by player count. Damage subtracts the attacker's ObjectBase.unk63 (plus the per-element modifier) from unk80. For food items (0x5E..0x64) it is the heal amount: the item's unk80 counts down one hp per 5 frames while healing, and it is also copied into kirby->unkE2. It also sets the power of the star Kirby spits after inhaling the type: (unk4 >> 1) + 9.

evidence.data: enemies 0x00..0x37: mostly 2 or 4; Rocky 5, Golems 7, Heavy Knight 8, Giant Rocky/Metal Guardian 10; Dark Mind Mirror 9999; boss rows hold roughly the 1-player HP but are not read as hp
evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

stats.summary: 1..10 for regular enemies; 9999 for OBJ_DARK_MIND_MIRROR (effectively unkillable)

fields.name: copyAbility
fields.description: Copy ability Kirby gets from inhaling the type (KIRBY_ABILITY_* value, 0 = none). Copied into Object.kirbyAbility (a u8) by InitObject; some constructors override it afterwards (Golem switches between Stone and Wheel, Droppy takes Kirby's, ability statues take subtype1 through their own tables).

evidence.data: 59 rows non-zero; e.g. Hot Head 1 (fire), Pengy 2 (ice), Sword Knight 18 (sword), Boxin 20 (fighter): match the in-game copy abilities
evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

fields.name: paletteSpec
fields.description: Object palette to load. Low 12 bits: the sprite (animId) whose palette is loaded with SpriteSomething, using the room record's unkF as the palette variant; the slot is looked up/allocated in the 7 dynamic OBJ palette slots (8..14). Bit 0x1000: the palette is reference-counted and released (sub_0803E4D4) when the object is destroyed, used by bosses/mini-bosses. 0 = shared palette 15. Objects flagged unkC & 0x10 (Droppy copies) use OBJ_DROPPY's entry instead.

sentinel.0: no own palette: use OBJ palette slot 15

packed.name: refcountedPalette
packed.description: release the palette slot on destroy

evidence.data: 64 rows are 0; 14 rows have bit 0x1000 (boss/mini-boss types); 97 distinct values
evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

fields.description: Alignment padding before the u32 numTiles (not a C member: the manifest names it pad0A). Zero in all 219 rows.

evidence.note: u32 at 0x0C forces 2 bytes of padding after unk8 at 0x08

evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

fields.name: vramTiles
fields.description: Number of 8x8 4bpp sprite tiles reserved in OBJ VRAM for one instance (VramMalloc). 0 = the type has no sprite (InitObject marks it flags 0x400|8). 0xFFFFFFFF = uses the fixed shared tile block at 0x06012000 (ability/warp stars, doors). It also picks the size of the star an inhaled object becomes (<9, <25, larger).

evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

fields.name: startState
fields.description: Function pointer: the type's first behaviour state. InitObject stores it as the object's current state function (Object.unk78, run every frame by ObjectMain); most constructors also call it once after setting up hitboxes and sprite. Two rows (0x96, 0x9A) are NULL. A ROM code address: the port binds these via generated rom_fn_tables.

evidence.data: 2 NULL rows; several types share a function (e.g. all Golems, all Moley projectiles)
evidence.tool: ROM read of gUnk_08351648 (scratch script, not in repo)

fields.name: animList
fields.description: Pointer to the type's AnimInfo list ({animId, variant}); Object.unk83 indexes it to pick the sprite animation; entry 0 is the default pose used when tiles are pre-decoded (sub_0803DD58). 8 rows NULL (sprite-less types).
